requested_result.rear: A real 3D rear base with one controllable manager character and toggleable first-person/third-person cameras.
requested_result.battlefield: A real 3D autonomous battlefield observed with a separate RTS camera supporting pan, zoom and inspection.
requested_result.completion: Migrate existing construction, acquisition, staffing, manufacturing, training, vehicles, physical logistics and autonomous battlefield behaviour; the first camera slice does not complete the overhaul.
requested_result.defaults: Manager physically remains in the rear. Preserve existing ground movement/terrain/visibility rules. Additional battlefield access, jumping, climbing, interiors, player combat and new elevation-based gameplay require an actual design decision rather than being inferred from 3D cameras.

non_negotiable_invariants: One live session, actual entity identities and authoritative state; no parallel 2D/3D workers, stock, requests, timers or moving copies.
Camera toggle changes perspective, not character identity, position, progress, assignment, cargo or time. Camera position never substitutes for player position.
Rear and battlefield retain intended progression when hidden. View transitions may prepare visual state but never replay elapsed gameplay, create duplicate jobs or stop hidden-world activity.
Keep actual claims, physical arrival/handling, exclusive people/crew, finite fuel, payload, cancellation/hold intent and receipt-versus-issue boundaries.
Approved normal opening remains paused, one manager, 2500 requisition, 500 M11, Supply Table/arrival, no hired workers/workshops/vehicles. Debug grants stay explicit separate actions.
Retain the 4000 by 6000 metre battlefield and existing army information restrictions. RTS observation does not issue military orders or reveal unknown enemies.
60 FPS remains a target to establish on declared hardware and workload; no claim that choosing 3D or using low-poly assets guarantees it. Existing performance and ordinary-loop gaps remain open.
Keep the current playable main until an integrated slice is reviewed and usable. Do not flip the default scene to an incomplete camera demonstration.

source_findings.finding: Control/_draw owns presentation AND current manager position/movement; extract player state ownership before adding camera modes. Existing WASD checks global keys and must not leak into menu or RTS input.
Control presentation uses ground Vector2 positions, 4000x6000 world bounds and existing selection/information policy. Replace rendering/picking without replacing policy.
Authoritative entity-local position is Vector2. Holder hierarchy, world positions and movement APIs are migration boundaries; resource counts/qualifications/ownership are dimension-independent.
add_place, move_entity, world-position/marker/colocation APIs are shared by logistics, combat and UI. A global textual Vector2-to-Vector3 replacement would corrupt ground axes and UI coordinates.

Existing ground/gradient/support and height-aware visibility already matter. probe constructs Vector3(map_x,map_y,height), not Godot's scene convention Vector3(x,height,z). Explicit axis conversion is mandatory.
Footprint, door, usable access, site/material and cancellation authority must remain shared between 3D preview and final placement. UI coordinates stay Vector2.
Current Control shell constructs one GameSession and rear/battlefield views. Reuse session/controllers; introduce a scene-owned 3D world/input composition rather than another autoload or simulation.
Current rendering method is GL Compatibility. Full 3D does not itself mandate a renderer change; choose renderer from actual visual requirements, hardware and CI feasibility.

architecture.state: Existing service owners keep authoritative economy, activities, people and physical custody. Extract manager pose from BaseMap into session-owned player state; scene controller publishes collision-resolved movement to that one state.
architecture.presentation: Scene-owned 3D world host and visible entity presenters bind by stable entity ID. Building/worker/vehicle models and animations consume committed state; displaying or hiding a model cannot manufacture, transfer or complete goods/work.
architecture.spatial_target: Metres; Godot X/Z ground plane and Y up. Planar geometry remains explicit ground projection where meaningful. Full migration uses one authoritative pose per entity, with any temporary legacy ground representation derived from it, never independently mutable.
architecture.temporary_boundary: First camera slice may adapt existing ground coordinates to scene Vector3(x,terrain_height,z). This is a staging boundary, not full overhaul completion. Before changing ledger types, record an owner-by-owner migration for local/holder/world poses, terrain probe axes, routes and all consumers; preserve existing terrain height/visibility semantics.
architecture.player: CharacterBody3D is the candidate for collision-resolved grounded player movement. One player body, separate camera rig modes; physics-step movement is legitimate continuous work, not a new logistics polling loop.
architecture.cameras: Third-person pivot/SpringArm3D/Camera3D for collision-aware following; first-person eye pivot with deliberate near-plane/body visibility handling; independent RTS Camera3D rig. A scene-owned mode/input owner arbitrates active camera, cursor and focus.
architecture.picking: Queue placement/selection queries from input and run physics-space reads at a safe physics boundary. Preview recomputes on aim/camera/rotation/geometry changes. Overlap signals can maintain occupancy candidates; authoritative commit still checks current footprint, resources and access once. No inventory/inspect_entity scan just because a blueprint is stationary.
architecture.navigation: NavigationServer3D is available for world routes where justified. Preserve current vehicle width, turning, fuel, access, bridge/load and cargo constraints explicitly; a navmesh path alone does not establish vehicle feasibility. Do not replace planar distance/heading with Vector3 distance silently: current slope/surface/rolling/bridge costs and accepted seconds/fuel must be reconciled without double charging. No per-frame repath or blanket NavigationAgent for every entity by default.
architecture.combat_and_information: Use existing permitted friendly markers and observed/stale enemy contacts, not true hidden ledger positions, for 3D models and picking. Existing terrain probes encode height, cover and range: convert axes deliberately. Generate visible walls/ramps/bridges/colliders from the same authoritative geometry. Mesh ray hits or animation muzzle sockets cannot silently replace current damage, friendly-line, range or cover rules; real new firing geometry is a separate accepted migration decision.
architecture.large_world: Bounded/chunked representation for the4x6km battlefield, not one scene node per metre. Preserve real distance/units; inspect close-camera precision and depth-range needs before selecting any floating-origin or double-precision solution.
architecture.events: Committed changes wake finite logistics/UI work; inventory/need projections remain event-owned. Active movement/camera interpolation and animation may update continuously using cached state. Paused/hidden presentation cannot become the simulation clock.
architecture.view_transition: Release latched input, preserve each camera's saved pose/selection and actual player pose, warm the destination presentation, then change view. Brief visual transition allowed; no catch-up simulation or world reset.

performance_and_verification.budget: 16.67ms/frame is the60FPS target, not a measured promise. Separate simulation, physics, render/animation and input costs; preserve raw outliers when later applicable evidence is collected.
performance_and_verification.design: Choose renderer after art/hardware requirements; preserve Compatibility baseline meanwhile. Use distance detail/visibility and suitable grouped repeated scenery; keep animation/physics bounded to required visible/active representations. Do not globally hide collision/terrain authority simply because a camera is elsewhere.
performance_and_verification.current_restrictions: No local Godot/native engine runs. No regression writing/suites, broad scenarios, failure matrices or benchmark campaigns. Each new feature may receive one brief expressly supplied GitHub current-change check/current-build visual capture within existing process bounds; source parsing is not gameplay acceptance.
performance_and_verification.limits: Software/headless CI may validate changed behaviour and appearance; target-hardware native input/FPS and ordinary whole-loop acceptance remain distinct. No thresholds increased and no old suite renamed as a direct check.
